_comment: Task 262 sub-task 1 — the RELATIONAL recall benchmark corpus.
Deliberately a hand-authored, committed, deterministic fixture (the Task-99
convention): every id the runner produces is a pure function of this file, so
two runs on two machines score identically. Fact TEXT is modelled on the shape
of this repo's own 2,300-fact corpus (short decision statements with a stated
mechanism), but the subject matter is a fictional service so nothing here
leaks project content into a fixture.
THE LOAD-BEARING PROPERTY. A `multi-hop` query's answer fact is written so it
does NOT contain the query's distinctive terms — it is reachable only by
following a `related:` edge out of the fact the query DOES match. Strip the
`related:` lists (the unlinked twin) and that answer becomes unreachable by
any flat pipeline. That is what makes the canary a real detector rather than
`supersededBy` clusters are deliberately NOT `related:` edges — they survive
the strip, so the `temporal` qtype is the control that proves a measured
margin is attributable to LINKING specifically and not to graph traversal in
general. `single-hop` + `preference` are the flat-answerable controls that
prove traversal does not REGRESS what already worked.

entries.title: Job transport, first generation
entries.body: Background jobs run through RabbitMQ with a dedicated worker fleet and one vhost per tenant.

entries.title: Durable consumers
entries.body: Durable consumers on NATS JetStream carry every asynchronous task; each subscriber acknowledges explicitly and redelivery stops after five attempts.

entries.title: Blue-green releases
entries.body: Releases go out blue-green behind the edge router, with traffic shifted in ten-percent steps.

entries.title: Stale colour retention
entries.body: The stale colour is retained for ninety minutes before teardown, so a regression can be undone without a rebuild.

entries.title: OIDC sign-in
entries.body: Sign-in uses OIDC against the corporate identity provider; local passwords were removed entirely.

entries.title: Where handshake material lives
entries.body: Material for the identity-provider handshake lives in the shared cache and never in a cookie.

entries.title: Dormancy eviction
entries.body: Cached handshake material is dropped after twenty minutes without activity, which forces a fresh exchange.

entries.title: Where uploads land
entries.body: Uploaded artefacts land in object storage under a per-tenant prefix.

entries.title: Object lifecycle
entries.body: Objects older than one year move to cold storage and are purged after seven years under the retention policy.

entries.title: Metric scraping
entries.body: Service metrics are scraped by Prometheus every fifteen seconds.

entries.title: Where pages go
entries.body: Pages reach the on-call rota through Opsgenie; anything below severity two only opens a ticket.

entries.title: API version support
entries.body: The public API is versioned in the path, and a version stays supported for eighteen months after its successor ships.

entries.title: Two warnings before shutdown
entries.body: Consumers are warned twice: a response header from the first day, then a direct mail six weeks before shutdown.

entries.title: Per-tenant allowance
entries.body: Every tenant gets a token bucket of six hundred requests per minute at the edge.

entries.title: Empty bucket behaviour
entries.body: When a bucket empties the edge answers 429 and sets Retry-After to the refill delay.

entries.title: Nightly backup
entries.body: A full backup runs nightly at 02:00 UTC into a separate account.

entries.title: Quarterly drill
entries.body: A restore is rehearsed every quarter against a scratch cluster, and the timing is recorded.

entries.title: Flag evaluation
entries.body: Feature flags are evaluated in-process from a snapshot refreshed every thirty seconds.

entries.title: Flag tidy-up
entries.body: A flag older than ninety days is reported to its owner and removed at the next tidy-up.

entries.title: Primary datastore, first generation
entries.body: The primary datastore is MySQL 8 with row-based replication.

entries.title: Every write path
entries.body: PostgreSQL 16 now backs every write path; logical replication feeds the read replicas.

entries.title: Full-text, first generation
entries.body: Full-text lookup runs on Solr with a nightly full import.

entries.title: Near-real-time indexing
entries.body: Elasticsearch replaced the nightly import and indexes in near real time.

entries.title: Rebuilt in under a minute
entries.body: Typesense serves every lookup today; its index is rebuilt from the source of record in under a minute.

entries.title: Base images, first generation
entries.body: Container images were Alpine-based with a shared build stage.

entries.title: Internal traffic, first generation
entries.body: Internal traffic was plain HTTP inside the VPC.

entries.title: Terse review comments
entries.body: Review comments should be terse: one line per finding, never a restatement of the diff.

entries.title: No emoji
entries.body: No emoji anywhere in generated output; plain text only.

entries.title: Shells that must work
entries.body: Every shell snippet must run on Windows PowerShell as well as POSIX shells.

entries.title: Merge queue
entries.body: Changes land through the GitHub merge queue; direct pushes to main are blocked.

entries.title: Implementation language
entries.body: The service is written in TypeScript with strict mode enabled everywhere.

entries.title: Test runner
entries.body: Tests run under Vitest, and a single npm script is the only supported entry point.

entries.title: Package manager
entries.body: Dependencies are installed with pnpm; the lockfile is pnpm-lock.yaml.

entries.title: Log format
entries.body: All logs are structured JSON with a request id on every line.

entries.title: Asset delivery
entries.body: Static assets are served from the CDN with a one-hour edge cache and immutable filenames.

entries.title: Purge trigger
entries.body: A purge is issued from the deploy pipeline whenever the asset manifest changes.

entries.title: Log retention
entries.body: Log volumes are kept hot for fourteen days and archived for one year.

entries.title: Secret delivery
entries.body: Secrets come from the vault at boot; nothing is baked into an image.

entries.title: Base images
entries.body: Container images are distroless and rebuilt weekly for patches.

entries.title: Service-to-service traffic
entries.body: Service-to-service traffic is mutual TLS with certificates rotated daily.

entries.title: Migration discipline
entries.body: Schema migrations run forward-only and must stay backward compatible for one release.

entries.title: Cloud budget
entries.body: Each team owns a monthly cloud budget and an alert fires at eighty percent.

entries.title: Locale coverage
entries.body: Nine locales ship today; strings are extracted at build time.

entries.title: Mobile client contract
entries.body: The mobile clients talk to the same public API and pin a minimum supported version.

entries.title: Support response times
entries.body: Support answers within one business day for standard plans and one hour for enterprise.

entries.title: Onboarding target
entries.body: A new engineer is productive in a week using the runbook index.

entries.title: Worker scaling signal
entries.body: Worker pods autoscale on queue depth rather than CPU.

entries.title: Analytics batching
entries.body: Product analytics events are batched client-side and flushed every thirty seconds.

entries.title: Postmortem rule
entries.body: Every severity-one incident gets a written postmortem within five business days.

entries.title: Release notes
entries.body: Release notes are generated from the changelog, never hand-written.
